title: Why Interactive Experiences Accelerate CX Transformation Faster Than Training
summary: Why Interactive Experiences Accelerate CX Transformation Faster Than Training
body_text: Modern video games don’t make you read a manual before you start to play. They drop players into a simulated world, give them simple objectives, and let them learn by doing. Even board games take the same approach, with cut-down quick-start versions and even free downloadable content to hook you in. That same principle explains why interactive experiences often drive better customer experience (CX) outcomes than traditional training. From Slides To Simulations At our recent CX Summit and Forums, participants built strategies, negotiated budgets, responded to executive challenges, and adapted to unexpected changes — in 50 minutes, all simulated. One participant told us, “We made more progress in 50 minutes than in months of real-world discussions.” The reason is simple: Simulations remove just enough real-world complexity to help people focus on decision-making. Rather than debating every organizational constraint, participants can experiment, collaborate, and see the consequences of their choices in real time. They build a mental model of success before returning to the realities of implementation. Design Experiences, Not Presentations Game design shows us how to get started and how to hook “ players ” : Start simple. Give participants clear goals before layering in complexity. Hand over control. Let teams make decisions rather than passively consume information. Simulate change. Create realistic scenarios that mirror the challenges of transformation. Interactive experiences also create something that presentations rarely achieve: emotional engagement. People remember the debate, the negotiation, the surprise challenge, and the ownership they felt over the outcome. Those experiences build confidence and alignment far more effectively than another strategy deck. If you want to accelerate CX transformation, stop asking how to improve the next presentation. Ask how you can help people explore, experiment, and learn together. The fastest path to change is often through play. You can learn more on the CX Cast episode, Hands On: Building Interactive Experiences , and if you are a Forrester client, check out our latest research on designing immersive experiences . Share

title: Avoiding Burnout as a Healthcare Provider
summary: Burnout is a reality many healthcare providers face, but it doesn't have to define your journey. Recognizing the signs—emotional exhaustion, detachment, and reduced effectiveness—is the first step toward reclaiming your well-being. At LunaJoy, we believe in empowering providers with practical strate
body_text: Burnout in healthcare is a growing concern, affecting not only healthcare workers but also the quality of patient care they provide. The demanding nature of your profession, coupled with emotional and physical health challenges, can lead to exhaustion, detachment, and decreased job performance. At LunaJoy, we understand the importance of supporting those who dedicate their lives to caring for others. Here’s how you can prioritize your well-being to avoid health worker burnout and thrive in your role. Recognizing the Signs of Burnout Identifying burnout early can help prevent it from escalating. Look out for: Emotional exhaustion: Feeling drained or overwhelmed . Depersonalization: A sense of disconnection from patients or colleagues. Reduced personal achievement: Struggling with feelings of ineffectiveness. Unaddressed, these symptoms can lead to more serious mental health problems or even substance abuse. If these symptoms resonate with you, it’s crucial to take proactive steps. Strategies for Preventing Burnout 1. Prioritize Self-Care Your health matters. Incorporate activities that recharge you: Exercise regularly to boost energy and reduce stress. Maintain a balanced diet to fuel your body and physical health. Practice mindfulness or meditation to center yourself. Establishing a healthy work-life balance is essential to sustaining energy and focus. 2. Set Boundaries Establishing boundaries is essential to prevent overwork: Limit after-hours tasks. Allow yourself to disconnect after shifts. Say no when necessary. Focus on tasks that align with your capacity. 3. Foster Supportive Relationships Cultivate connections that provide emotional support: Engage with peers. Sharing experiences can alleviate feelings of isolation. Seek mentorship. Guidance from experienced colleagues can offer perspective. 4. Embrace Professional Development Enhancing your skills can renew your passion for your profession: Attend workshops or online courses related to your field. Explore specializations that align with your interests. 5. Leverage Resources Take advantage of support systems available to you: Mental health services. Access therapy or counseling to manage stress. Employee assistance programs (EAPs). These often include resources like stress management training. Your healthcare employers play a key role in providing these tools. If support is lacking, it’s important to advocate for the resources you need. How LunaJoy Supports Healthcare Providers At LunaJoy , we offer: Virtual therapy and counseling: Convenient and confidential mental health support tailored to busy professionals. Workshops on stress management: Learn practical tools to handle chronic workplace stress effectively. Holistic care approaches: Address your mental, emotional, and physical health. Final Thoughts As a healthcare worker, your role is essential in ensuring quality patient care and delivering high-quality care. Prioritizing your well-being improves not only your job satisfaction but also the experiences of your patients. Recognizing the warning signs of healthcare burnout early can lead to effective solutions and help in reducing burnout risks. Burnout is not a sign of weakness—it’s a sign that something needs to change. By taking intentional steps to care for yourself, you can rediscover the joy and fulfillment that brought you to this profession in the first place.

body_text: Crescent Biopharma Announces Pricing of Public Offering of Ordinary Shares and Pre-Funded Warrants July 14, 2026 PDF Version WALTHAM, Mass., July 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Crescent Biopharma, Inc. (“Crescent” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: CBIO), a clinical-stage biotechnology company dedicated to rapidly advancing the next wave of therapies for cancer patients, today announced the pricing of its underwritten public offering of 8,094,793 ordinary shares and in lieu of ordinary shares to certain investors, pre-funded warrants to purchase up to 525,897 ordinary shares. The ordinary shares are being sold to the public at a price of $14.50 per share and the pre-funded warrants are being sold at a price to the public of $14.499 per pre-funded warrant, which represents the per ordinary share price less the $0.001 per share exercise price for each such pre-funded warrant. title: Improving Military Equipment Accountability with Real-Time Asset Tracking
body_text: Military organizations manage an extraordinary volume of equipment. Weapons cases, communications equipment, tactical radios, night vision devices, ammunition containers, maintenance kits, medical equipment, generators, drones, batteries, repair parts, and mission-specific gear are constantly moving between armories, warehouses, maintenance facilities, vehicles, aircraft, ships, and training areas. Maintaining accountability for these assets is essential to mission readiness. Yet across many installations, equipment management still relies heavily on manual inventories, barcode scans, sign-out procedures, and periodic inspections. These systems establish accountability at specific points in time, but they often provide limited visibility once equipment begins moving. Juxta's NODE1 asset tag was built to close that gap, providing continuous, real-time visibility into mission-critical equipment wherever it moves across a military installation or operational environment. Knowing Where Equipment Is—Without Waiting for the Next Inventory Military logistics depends on accountability. Before every mission, deployment, or training exercise, personnel need confidence that critical equipment is available, serviceable, and located where it is expected to be. Unfortunately, equipment is constantly changing hands. A communications kit may move from an armory to a training range, then to a maintenance shop before being issued to another unit. Specialized tools may be shared between maintenance teams. Medical equipment may support multiple exercises in a single week. Portable generators, drone systems, and testing equipment are routinely reassigned based on operational priorities. Manual inventories capture only snapshots of this activity. NODE1 provides continuous visibility between those snapshots, allowing logistics teams to understand where equipment is throughout its lifecycle instead of only where it was last recorded. Built for High-Value Military Assets NODE1 is a compact, rechargeable asset tag designed to attach directly to equipment that moves frequently throughout military operations. Common applications include: Weapons cases Tactical radios Night vision equipment Unmanned aircraft systems Counter-UAS equipment Portable communications kits Medical kits Generators Power distribution equipment Toolkits Test and calibration equipment Ammunition containers Electronic warfare equipment Mission support equipment Specialized maintenance tools Rather than relying on manual tracking, each tagged asset becomes continuously visible as it moves across the installation. Reducing Time Spent Searching Few activities consume more time than searching for equipment needed immediately. A maintenance crew may spend valuable time locating specialized test equipment before beginning repairs. An aviation unit may need to identify the nearest power cart before preparing an aircraft. A communications team may search multiple storage rooms for a deployable radio kit scheduled for a training exercise later that morning. Individually, these searches may take only a few minutes. Across thousands of personnel and countless daily operations, those minutes become significant lost productivity. With NODE1, personnel can quickly locate required equipment instead of relying on phone calls, manual inventories, or institutional knowledge. Improving Equipment Utilization Military organizations frequently manage more equipment than they have visibility into. Without objective utilization data, it can be difficult to determine whether additional procurement is truly necessary or whether existing equipment is simply unevenly distributed across units. NODE1 provides operational insight into questions such as: Which equipment is used most frequently? Which assets remain idle for extended periods? Where does equipment typically accumulate? How often are assets transferred between units? Which mission kits are consistently deployed? Which resources rarely leave storage? These data help logistics officers make more informed decisions about procurement, redistribution, and long-term equipment planning. Supporting Armories and Supply Operations Armories and military supply facilities manage thousands of controlled assets with strict accountability requirements. While sign-out procedures remain essential, they provide limited visibility after equipment leaves the facility. By attaching NODE1 directly to mission-critical equipment, logistics personnel gain continuous awareness of asset movement while equipment is deployed, staged for operations, undergoing maintenance, or awaiting reissue. Historical movement records also provide additional operational insight into how equipment circulates across an installation over time. Improving Maintenance Operations Maintenance organizations depend on both equipment availability and efficient workflows. Ground support equipment, calibration instruments, specialized diagnostic tools, and repair kits frequently move between maintenance bays, aircraft, vehicles, and storage facilities. When these resources cannot be located quickly, maintenance schedules are delayed despite having the necessary equipment on base. NODE1 enables maintenance teams to identify equipment locations immediately, reducing search time while improving overall workflow efficiency. Maintenance leaders also gain historical movement data that helps optimize equipment distribution across maintenance facilities. Supporting Training and Readiness Training exercises require significant quantities of shared equipment to move between storage facilities, vehicles, ranges, classrooms, and operational training areas. Keeping track of these assets throughout preparation, execution, and recovery is often labor-intensive. NODE1 simplifies this process by providing continuous visibility before, during, and after training events. Units can verify that mission-essential equipment has arrived where expected, identify resources that remain staged at previous locations, and streamline post-exercise accountability without relying solely on manual inventories. Integrating Into Existing Logistics Systems NODE1 is designed to complement existing military logistics systems rather than replace them. Location data can be integrated into logistics platforms, inventory management software, maintenance systems, enterprise resource planning applications, and custom operational dashboards. This allows commanders and logistics personnel to combine inventory records with live equipment locations, creating a more complete picture of operational readiness. Instead of knowing only what equipment has been assigned, organizations gain visibility into where those assets are throughout their operational lifecycle. Built for Military Environments Military equipment operates under demanding conditions. Assets are transported between bases, loaded into aircraft, stored aboard ships, deployed in field environments, and repeatedly moved during training and operational missions. NODE1 was designed for these conditions. Its compact, rechargeable form factor allows it to be securely attached to a wide variety of military equipment while supporting continuous visibility across installations, maintenance facilities, training areas, and operational environments. Whether supporting installation logistics, aviation maintenance, ground vehicle operations, communications units, or expeditionary forces, the platform provides a consistent layer of asset visibility. Strengthening Equipment Accountability Across the Force Operational readiness depends on more than owning the right equipment. It depends on being able to locate it quickly, deploy it efficiently, and understand how it is being used. By attaching NODE1 asset tags directly to tactical gear, mission equipment, maintenance assets, and deployable systems, defense organizations gain continuous visibility into resources that are traditionally managed through periodic inventories alone. That visibility helps reduce time spent searching for equipment, improves accountability, increases asset utilization, supports maintenance operations, and provides logistics leaders with better data for planning and resource allocation. As military operations become increasingly data-driven, continuous equipment visibility offers a practical way to strengthen readiness while making better use of the assets already in service. ‍

title: William Blair Internship 2027–2028: Programs, Deadlines & How to Apply
summary: Land a William Blair internship in 2027–2028: 6 tracks, $1,920/week + $5K housing, timeline, HireVue-to-Superday interview loop with paper LBO, and tips.
body_text: William Blair Internship 2027–2028: Programs, Deadlines & How to Apply Last updated: July 2026 William Blair interns earn $1,920 per week (annualized ~$99,840) plus a $5,000 housing stipend, placing the firm's compensation on par with bulge-bracket banks despite its middle-market positioning. The IB Summer Analyst class is intimate at 10 to 20 seats across eight offices, and the firm's 100% employee-owned partnership structure creates a culture where, as multiple reviews put it, they hire 'people who will one day run the firm.' For the 2027–2028 cycle, applications are expected to open as early as March 2027, following the accelerated IB recruiting trend. Quick Facts Fact Detail Where to apply williamblair.com/Careers . Also check Handshake and on-campus boards. Contact: campusrecruiting@williamblair.com Application window (2027–28) Expected March to June 2027 for Summer 2028 IB roles. HireVue assessments June to August 2027. Superdays August to November 2027. Offers September to December 2027. Projected from prior cycles Rolling? Yes. William Blair reviews applications on a rolling basis. For on-campus partners, specific deadlines are posted on school career sites. Apply as early as possible Eligibility Rising seniors for IB Summer Analyst. Rising sophomores, juniors, or seniors for PWM and other tracks. GPA 3.5+ preferred. All universities considered, no strict target-school requirement Duration 9 to 10 weeks for IB Summer Analyst (June to August). 6 to 12 weeks depending on program track Compensation $1,920 per week (~$99,840 annualized) for IB Summer Analysts. $5,000 housing stipend plus up to $1,200 domestic relocation. Dinner stipend and car service for late nights in Chicago Visa sponsorship William Blair will consider candidates who may require sponsorship; however, requirements vary by role. Check specific postings or contact recruiters directly Locations IB: Atlanta, Boston, Charlotte, Chicago (HQ), London, Los Angeles, New York, San Francisco. PWM: 8 US cities. IM, Equities, WiT: Chicago only # Programs 6+ tracks: IB Summer Analyst, Investment Management, Equity Research/Sales & Trading, Private Wealth Management, Working in Technology (WiT), plus Frankfurt Off-Cycle and Bridge to IB diversity program Two numbers frame the opportunity: $1,920 per week plus $5,000 housing at a Vault Banking Top 25 firm, with a 72 to 82% return-offer rate. William Blair reviews applications on a rolling basis, and the accelerated IB recruiting timeline means the spring 2027 opening date is the sharpest edge you have. Externships are short, remote projects where you finish real work for a real company. The Wayfair AI Agent Engineering Externship and Beats by Dre Data Analytics Externship build the quantitative reasoning, data fluency, and analytical evidence a William Blair application and its paper-LBO-heavy interviews reward. Explore all Externships . What Is a William Blair Internship? A William Blair internship is a paid, full-time placement at one of the last remaining 100% employee-owned independent investment banks on Wall Street. The flagship IB Summer Analyst program runs 9 to 10 weeks and places interns into specialized industry groups including Technology, Healthcare, Consumer & Retail, Business Services, Financial Services, and Industrials. Unlike large-bank programs where interns may spend weeks on pitchbooks alone, William Blair's smaller class of 10 to 20 means direct exposure to live M&A transactions, public equity offerings, and private placements alongside senior bankers from day one. The firm manages approximately $80 billion in client assets and $65 billion in regulatory AUM, and its growth-equity-meets-traditional-M&A positioning in the middle market has earned it Vault Banking Top 25 status and a 4.3 out of 5.0 Glassdoor rating across 547+ reviews. Approximately 72 to 82% of interns receive full-time return offers. When Do William Blair Internship Applications Open for 2027–2028? William Blair's IB recruiting follows the accelerated investment-banking timeline that has shifted earlier each year. For the Summer 2028 cycle, applications are expected to open as early as March 2027, with HireVue assessments due by June to August 2027, first-round interviews running June through September, Superdays August through November, and offers extending on a rolling basis through December. Non-IB programs (Private Wealth, Investment Management, Equities, WiT) typically recruit on a later timeline. The critical insight: William Blair reviews applications on a rolling basis, and the firm officially notes that for students at partner schools, specific deadlines are posted on school career sites, so missing those deadlines means competing in a later, more crowded pool. Now · Summer 2026 YOU ARE HERE Summer 2028 IB postings are not yet live. This is the build window: master paper LBO mechanics, develop your 'Why William Blair?' narrative around the employee-owned partnership and middle-market growth focus, and research the firm's industry groups (Technology, Healthcare, Consumer & Retail). The Wayfair AI Agent Engineering Externship and the Beats by Dre Data Analytics Externship are remote, real-company projects that give a spring 2027 application finished, analytical work to point at. March to June 2027 EXPECTED ROLLING — APPLY WEEK 1 IB Summer Analyst applications expected to open. Apply through williamblair.com/Careers, Handshake, or your school's on-campus portal as soon as postings appear. Begin networking with William Blair employees and attending info sessions. June to August 2027 EXPECTED HireVue video assessments due. 3 to 5 questions, 20 to 30 minutes, primarily behavioral with occasional technical. First-round phone/video interviews begin (30 minutes with analysts and associates, 50% behavioral, 50% technical). August to November 2027 EXPECTED Superday interviews at Chicago HQ or regional offices. 4 to 5 back-to-back 30-minute interviews: one pure-technical with Associate featuring the signature paper LBO, one pure-behavioral with MD testing judgment and maturity, and 2 to 3 mixed rounds with VPs and Directors. Offers extend on a rolling basis. June to August 2028 9 to 10 weeks, full-time. Work on live M&A, equity offerings, and private placements. Mid-program review at week 5, end-of-program review in the final week, then return-offer decisions. Perform well and the 72 to 82% conversion rate becomes your number. Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open Rolling review is the mechanism, not a footnote. William Blair reviews applications as they arrive, and the firm's official guidance tells students at partner schools to watch for specific deadlines on campus career sites, implying that these deadlines are real cutoffs, not suggestions. With the accelerated IB recruiting trend pushing timelines earlier each year, applying in March or April 2027, as soon as applications open, gives you the widest pool of available seats. Later applicants face fewer remaining positions and tighter competition. Beyond timing, the 'Why Blair?' question carries unusual weight: interviewers go deep on this, and vague answers about 'culture' or 'middle market' do not pass. You need a specific answer about the employee-owned partnership structure, a particular industry group you want to join, or a recent deal that drew your interest. Prepare that answer now, while you have time to make it authentic. Which William Blair Internship Programs Should You Target? William Blair offers six distinct internship tracks across its campus recruiting platform, plus additional diversity and off-cycle programs. Each track has its own timeline, location footprint, and eligibility requirements. The IB Summer Analyst is the flagship, but the other tracks provide entry points for candidates interested in buy-side investing, equity research, wealth management, or technology. Program Focus Duration Key skills IB Summer Analyst Growth-oriented M&A advisory and capital raising for middle-market companies across Technology, Healthcare, Consumer & Retail, Business Services, Financial Services, and Industrials 9–10 weeks Financial modeling (DCF, LBO, comps), Excel, pitchbook preparation, industry research, client communication Investment Management Intern Buy-side fundamental analysis supporting portfolio managers across ~$65B AUM in US equity, non-US equity, and emerging markets strategies 6–8 weeks Equity research, fundamental analysis, financial statement analysis, portfolio construction Equity Research / Sales & Trading Intern Institutional equity sales processes covering 700+ companies across seven sectors. Includes stock-pitch competition 6–8 weeks Equity analysis, market knowledge, communication, presentation skills Private Wealth Management Intern Advising HNW individuals, families, and endowments. Choose between client-service and middle-office-operations tracks 8 weeks Client service, financial planning, portfolio analysis, relationship management Working in Technology (WiT) Intern Diversity-focused tech internship: app development, data science, project management, platform engineering 10–12 weeks Cloud computing, software development, data science, business analytics Frankfurt Off-Cycle IB Intern 3-month generalist IB program with quarterly intakes (January, April, July, October) in the Frankfurt office 3 months Financial modeling, M&A mechanics, European market knowledge, German language helpful See every open role on the William Blair campus recruiting portal . Note the diversity pipeline: the Bridge to Investment Banking Program targets female sophomores, and the WiT program explicitly recruits from underrepresented backgrounds in technology. PWM accepts rising sophomores, making it the earliest entry point across all tracks. What Are the Eligibility Requirements? William Blair's requirements vary by track, but these lines repeat across most postings: • Year: rising seniors for IB Summer Analyst. Rising sophomores, juniors, or seniors for PWM (the earliest entry point). Rising juniors and seniors for Investment Management and Equities. • Degree: pursuing a Bachelor's (BA or BS) or MBA. Finance, economics, and accounting preferred for IB, but no strict major requirement is stated. • GPA: 3.5+ cumulative preferred. Not a hard cutoff, but a consistent threshold across postings. • Universities: William Blair officially 'considers candidates from all universities,' with stronger on-campus pipelines at Midwest targets (UIUC, Michigan, Northwestern, Chicago Booth, Indiana Kelley, Notre Dame Mendoza, Wisconsin) and national targets. • Work authorization: William Blair will consider candidates who may require sponsorship; however, requirements vary by role. Check specific postings or contact campusrecruiting@williamblair.com. Does William Blair Have Diversity-Specific Programs? Yes, and they are worth targeting. The Bridge to Investment Banking Program specifically recruits female sophomores for future IB internships. The Working in Technology (WiT) program explicitly targets high-performing individuals from underrepresented backgrounds in technology. The firm earned a top score on the Human Rights Campaign Foundation's 2026 Corporate Equality Index for the fifth consecutive year and six consecutive USA Top Workplaces honors. Internal employee resource groups include the Women's Alliance, Pride Alliance, Veterans' Alliance, and ONE Alliance. What Skills Does William Blair Look For, and How Do You Build Them? Read across William Blair intern job descriptions spanning the IB Summer Analyst, Investment Management, Equities, PWM, and WiT tracks, and the pattern is clear. Communication and analytical thinking appear in all six, financial modeling in four, Excel proficiency in four, and industry knowledge in three. But the skill list only tells half the story. William Blair's Superday features a signature paper LBO that appears at almost every stage, and the firm's 'Why Blair?' question is probed with unusual depth. Interviewers test whether you genuinely understand the employee-owned partnership model and can articulate why you want this firm specifically, not just any middle-market bank. Bring the modeling, then wrap every story in cultural fit and judgment. What William Blair looks for in interns Skills across 6 William Blair intern & analyst job descriptions · 2025–26 cycle William Blair intern JDs across IB, IM, Equities, PWM, WiT, and off-cycle tracks, projecting 2027–2028 Communication & analytical thinking 6 of 6 Financial modeling (DCF, LBO, comps, accretion/dilution) 4 of 6 Excel proficiency & quantitative reasoning 4 of 6 Industry knowledge (technology, healthcare, consumer) 3 of 6 Accounting fundamentals (three statements) 3 of 6 Client service & relationship management 3 of 6 Equity research & fundamental analysis 2 of 6 Data science & software development (WiT) 1 of 6 Method: full-text analysis of six William Blair intern job descriptions across IB Summer Analyst, Investment Management, Equity Research/Sales & Trading, Private Wealth Management, Working in Technology, and Frankfurt Off-Cycle tracks. Prior-cycle basis; cultural fit and the paper LBO are evaluated in dedicated interview rounds rather than listed as JD qualifications. How Is Demand for Investment Banking Summer Analysts Moving Right Now? Build These Skills Before You Apply And every skill in that chart maps to a remote Externship where you finish a real project before a role opens. Skill (from real JDs) JD evidence Externship that builds it Quantitative modeling & analytical reasoning IB JDs: "build financial models (DCF, LBO, accretion/dilution, comparable company analyses)" and "conduct industry and company research" Wayfair AI Agent Engineering Data analysis, metrics interpretation & research IM and Equities JDs: "conduct fundamental investment analysis" and "support portfolio managers and research analysts" Beats by Dre Data Analytics Communication & cross-functional presentation All JDs: "prepare pitchbooks and client presentations" and "attend client meetings and participate in deal processes" Wayfair AI Agent Engineering How close is the overlap? The Wayfair project is analytical engineering work that yields the build-and-explain evidence William Blair's Superday and paper LBO probe for, and the Beats project ends on the data-analysis story a behavioral round wants. What Is the William Blair Application and Interview Process Like? William Blair's funnel spans four stages from application to offer: 1. Apply on williamblair.com/Careers . Search for IB Summer Analyst or other tracks, select your preferred location(s), and submit resume, cover letter, and transcript. Multiple position and location applications are permitted. For on-campus partner schools, watch for specific deadlines on your school's career site. 2. Complete the HireVue video assessment (20 to 30 minutes). A one-way recorded video with 3 to 5 questions and 30 to 60 seconds of prep time per question. Primarily behavioral: Tell me about yourself, Why investment banking?, Why William Blair specifically?, a teamwork experience. Occasional technical questions on financial statement analysis or enterprise value. Aim for concise 60- to 90-second answers with direct camera eye contact. 3. First-round interviews (30 minutes each). Phone or video calls with analysts and associates, approximately 50% behavioral and 50% technical. Technical topics include DCF walkthrough, enterprise value versus equity value, and basic accounting. The 'Why Blair?' question is critical: they go deep and expect a real answer about the independent partnership structure, culture of accountability, or a specific industry group. 4. Superday (final round, in-person). 4 to 5 back-to-back 30-minute interviews at Chicago HQ or a regional office. One pure-technical with an Associate featuring the signature paper LBO with pushback on assumptions. One pure-behavioral with an MD testing judgment, maturity, and ethical reasoning. 2 to 3 mixed rounds with VPs and Directors. Return-offer decisions arrive in the final week of the internship, informed by both mid-program and end-of-program reviews. So the two skills to drill are clear: paper-LBO fluency (walk through sources and uses, build an income-statement bridge, calculate IRR and MOIC by hand, identify value-creation levers, and handle pushback gracefully) and a genuine, specific 'Why Blair?' narrative. The paper LBO is William Blair's defining interview exercise, appearing at almost every stage, and the firm's emphasis on cultural fit means a strong technical candidate with a vague motivation answer will not advance. Prepare both, and practice the LBO without a calculator until it is automatic. What Students on Reddit Say Three community threads show the process from the inside, all paraphrased. When preparing for a William Blair IB analyst interview, candidates are advised to go especially deep on the 'Why William Blair?' question and to master standard technical prep, since Blair interviewers expect specificity about the firm's independent partnership and culture that generic answers cannot satisfy. r/FinancialCareers interview prep, paraphrased · read the thread IB summer analyst recruiting at firms like William Blair is described as ridiculously early, with many candidates reporting that by summer, recruiting for the following year is often already wrapped up. The consensus is to apply during the spring semester the year before your target internship. r/FinancialCareers recruiting timeline, paraphrased · read the thread William Blair is cited alongside Houlihan Lokey as a top middle-market IB target, with commenters noting that breaking into these firms without a traditional summer analyst path requires significant networking and demonstrated technical preparation, but the smaller class sizes mean more direct deal exposure than bulge brackets. r/FinancialCareers firm reputation, paraphrased · read the thread How Do You Stand Out at a Firm That Hires People to Run It? Three moves, all before a role opens. First, apply in the first week of the March or April 2027 opening: rolling review plus the accelerated IB timeline means timing and prep beat prestige, and William Blair officially considers candidates from all universities, so non-target applicants who apply early face a wider pool of available seats. Second, master the paper LBO cold: walk through sources and uses from memory, calculate IRR and MOIC by hand without a calculator, identify key drivers (revenue growth, margin expansion, multiple expansion, debt paydown), and practice handling pushback on your assumptions, because the paper LBO is William Blair's signature exercise and it appears at almost every interview stage. Third, build a genuine 'Why Blair?' answer backed by specific knowledge: reference the employee-owned partnership structure, name the industry group you want to join (Technology, Healthcare, Consumer & Retail), and cite a recent deal that drew your interest. The pure-behavioral MD round tests judgment and maturity, not just motivation, so prepare situational and ethical scenarios too. And remember: 72 to 82% of interns get return offers, so interview like the full-time seat is already on the table. What Other Companies Should You Consider? William Blair is not the only middle-market bank recruiting on an accelerated calendar. If you are building an IB internship list that balances prestige with deal exposure, these are the obvious neighbors: Houlihan Lokey Middle-market leader in restructuring and financial advisory with comparable deal exposure and cultural emphasis Guide → Piper Sandler Middle-market IB with strength in healthcare, technology, and financial services sectors Guide → Robert W. Baird Employee-owned Midwest rival with strong middle-market M&A and equity research platforms Guide → Goldman Sachs Bulge-bracket benchmark with larger cohorts and broader coverage but less per-intern deal exposure Guide → JPMorgan Bulge-bracket giant with extensive training programs and rotational options across divisions Guide → Our finance internships summer 2027 guide maps the whole landscape, timeline by timeline. FAQ When do William Blair IB internship applications open for summer 2028? Expect IB Summer Analyst applications to open as early as March 2027, with HireVue assessments due June to August 2027, Superdays August to November 2027, and offers extending through December 2027. Those dates are projected from prior cycles and follow the accelerated IB recruiting trend. Set a job alert on williamblair.com/Careers. Is William Blair internship hiring rolling? Yes. William Blair reviews applications on a rolling basis. For students at on-campus partner schools, specific deadlines are posted on school career sites. The firm notes you should expect to hear back 'in the months following your submission,' so applying early maximizes your chances. How much does a William Blair IB internship pay? IB Summer Analysts earn $1,920 per week (~$99,840 annualized) for 9 to 10 weeks, plus a $5,000 housing stipend and up to $1,200 in domestic relocation. The firm also provides dinner stipends for late work and car service for late nights in Chicago. This places compensation on par with bulge-bracket rates. Does William Blair sponsor visas for interns? William Blair states it will consider candidates who may require sponsorship; however, requirements vary by role. International students should check specific job descriptions for sponsorship eligibility and contact campusrecruiting@williamblair.com directly to confirm. What is the William Blair Superday like? The Superday is an in-person round of 4 to 5 back-to-back 30-minute interviews. One interview is pure technical with an Associate featuring a paper LBO with pushback on assumptions. One is pure behavioral with an MD testing judgment and ethical reasoning. The remaining 2 to 3 are mixed behavioral and technical with VPs and Directors. How should I prepare for the paper LBO? The paper LBO is William Blair's signature interview exercise. Memorize the LBO structure (sources and uses, income statement, debt schedule, returns calculation). Practice calculating IRR and MOIC by hand without a calculator. Understand the key value-creation levers (revenue growth, margin expansion, multiple expansion, debt paydown). Prepare to handle pushback on your assumptions gracefully. Do I need to be at a target school? No. William Blair officially considers candidates from all universities. However, the firm has stronger on-campus pipelines at Midwest targets (UIUC, Michigan, Northwestern, Chicago Booth, Indiana Kelley, Notre Dame, Wisconsin) and national targets. Non-target candidates should network proactively and apply through the online portal. What is the return-offer rate? Approximately 72 to 82% of interns convert to full-time offers. Return decisions are delivered in the final week of the internship, informed by both a mid-program review (around week 5) and an end-of-program review. William Blair's employee-owned culture means they hire people to run the firm, and every internship seat is an audition for that future. Spend the runway building proof: a remote Externship turns 'interested in middle-market IB' into a finished project you can point at when recruiting opens. About the Author Bifei Wang has spent 17 years focused on human flow and the growth of young professionals, spanning international education, career training and coaching, and recruitment process outsourcing. Over 7 years at Extern, he has had one-on-one sessions with thousands of students exploring careers in consulting, finance, tech, marketing, and data, giving him a firsthand view of how the job market has shifted for early-career professionals and what it actually takes to break in.

title: Are Union Dues Tax Deductible? What Construction Contractors and Workers Need to Know
summary: Union dues are no longer deductible on federal returns for W-2 workers. See who can still deduct, which states allow it, and how payroll should handle dues.
body_text: Union dues are a fact of life for contractors and workers on union jobsites. Whether those dues are deductible at tax time is a question that comes up every filing season, and the answer changed significantly after 2017 and then changed again in 2025. For construction workers filing W-2s and contractors managing union payroll, understanding the current rules prevents costly mistakes on returns and keeps payroll deduction codes set up correctly. The short answer for 2026: union dues are not deductible on federal income tax returns for most W-2 employees. The longer answer involves a few important exceptions, state-level variations, and a distinction between what workers can deduct and what contractors can deduct as employers. Consult a qualified tax professional for guidance specific to your situation, as tax laws are subject to change and individual circumstances vary. Federal Tax Rules on Union Dues for Construction Workers and Contractors Prior to 2018, union members who itemized their federal tax returns could deduct union dues as a miscellaneous itemized deduction on Schedule A, subject to a 2% adjusted gross income (AGI) floor. The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) of 2017 suspended that entire category of deductions for tax years 2018 through 2025. Many union workers expected the deduction to return in 2026 when the TCJA provisions were set to expire. The deduction did not come back. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21), signed into law in July 2025, removed the sunset date from Internal Revenue Code Section 67(g), making the elimination of miscellaneous itemized deductions, including union dues, permanent. For W-2 construction workers, union dues paid to locals, international unions, or trade councils are no longer deductible on federal tax returns, and no scheduled date exists for the deduction to return under current law. Who Can Still Deduct Union Dues on a Federal Return While the general federal deduction is gone for W-2 employees, two narrow categories of filers can still claim union dues. Self-employed construction workers. Independent contractors and sole proprietors who pay union dues as part of their business operations can deduct those dues as an ordinary and necessary business expense on Schedule C (Form 1040) . For a self-employed electrician or pipefitter who maintains union membership to access work through the hiring hall, the dues are a direct cost of doing business and remain fully deductible. Certain statutory employees. Qualified performing artists, fee-basis state and local government employees, and Armed Forces reservists can still deduct unreimbursed business expenses, including union dues, using Form 2106. Most construction workers do not fall into these categories. For the vast majority of union construction workers who receive a W-2, the federal deduction is not available. State-Level Deductions That May Still Apply Even though the federal deduction is gone, some states did not conform to the TCJA and still allow workers to deduct union dues on their state income tax returns. State rules vary significantly, and eligibility typically requires itemizing on the state return rather than taking the state standard deduction. For union construction workers in states that allow the deduction, the savings depend on the state's tax rate and the total dues paid during the year. Union dues in construction typically range from 1% to 2% of gross wages, which can amount to several hundred to over a thousand dollars annually for full-time workers. States that generally allow union dues deductions include: New York: Allows an itemized deduction for union dues on state returns California: Did not conform to the TCJA; union dues may be deductible on state returns Pennsylvania: Typically allows employees to deduct union dues from state income Minnesota: Generally allows residents to deduct union dues on state returns States with no income tax (Texas, Florida, Washington, Nevada, Wyoming, Tennessee, South Dakota, Alaska, New Hampshire) do not have a state return on which to claim the deduction. Most other states have conformed to the federal TCJA and do not allow the deduction. For contractors running ​ multi-state payroll , understanding which states allow the deduction matters for employee communications, not for payroll withholding. The deduction is claimed on the employee's state return, not through payroll. How Union Dues Work in Construction Payroll Union dues are typically withheld from employee paychecks as after-tax deductions. Federal income tax, state income tax, Social Security, and Medicare are calculated first on the gross wage, then union dues are subtracted from the remaining amount. Because the dues are not deductible at the federal level, they do not reduce taxable wages for income tax purposes. Payroll teams should verify that union dues deduction codes are set up as after-tax, not pre-tax, in the payroll system. A misconfigured deduction code that treats dues as pre-tax would understate federal taxable wages and create withholding errors that compound across every pay period until caught. For contractors managing crews across multiple union locals, each with different dues structures, the configuration needs to be correct per local and per worker. Employers may choose to report union dues in Box 14a of the W-2 . Box 14 is an informational field used for items that do not have a dedicated box elsewhere on the form. Reporting union dues in Box 14 is optional but helpful for workers who need to verify total dues paid for state tax returns or personal records. A ​ construction payroll system that handles union deductions alongside prevailing wage calculations, fringe benefit contributions, and multi-state withholding ensures that dues are processed correctly without manual adjustments each pay period. What Contractors Can Deduct on the Employer Side The rules for employers are different from the rules for employees. Union dues paid by workers are not deductible on the worker's federal return, but employer obligations related to union labor are treated as deductible business expenses for the contractor. Employer-side costs that remain deductible include: Fringe benefit fund contributions. Employer contributions to union health, pension, annuity, vacation, and training trust funds, made per the collective bargaining agreement, are deductible as ordinary business expenses. Workers' compensation premiums. Premiums paid on union and non-union employees alike are deductible business expenses. Employer payroll taxes. The employer's share of Social Security, Medicare, and federal and state unemployment taxes on union workers' wages is deductible. The distinction matters: worker-side union dues are not deductible for the worker, but employer-side labor costs, including CBA-mandated fringe contributions, remain fully deductible for the contractor. How to Keep Union Dues Records Organized Even though the federal deduction is not available for W-2 workers, maintaining accurate records of union dues paid throughout the year is still important for several reasons. Workers in states that allow state-level deductions need documentation to support their claim. Self-employed workers deducting on Schedule C need clear records separating dues from personal expenses. And in the event of a payroll audit or workers' comp review, accurate records of all deductions, including union dues, help demonstrate that payroll was processed correctly. For contractors, clean records of union dues withheld per employee support accurate W-2 reporting , fringe benefit reconciliation, and audit readiness. A payroll and HR system that tracks union membership status, dues withholding, and CBA-specific deductions for each worker in one place reduces the year-end reconciliation burden when W-2s are generated. Handle Union Payroll Complexity in One System Trayd processes union dues deductions, fringe benefit contributions, prevailing wage calculations, and multi-state withholding in a single ​ construction payroll platform . When union deduction codes, CBA rate schedules, and worker classifications are managed in the same system that runs payroll, the data stays clean through every pay period without manual workarounds. ​ Schedule a demo to see how union payroll works in Trayd. Frequently Asked Questions Are union dues tax-deductible in 2026? For W-2 employees, no. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act made the elimination of the federal union dues deduction permanent starting in 2026. Self-employed workers can still deduct union dues on Schedule C as a business expense, and some states allow deductions on state tax returns. Why did union dues stop being deductible? The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 suspended the deduction for miscellaneous itemized deductions, including union dues, for tax years 2018 through 2025. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act, signed in July 2025, removed the sunset date, making the suspension permanent. Can self-employed construction workers deduct union dues? Yes. Independent contractors and sole proprietors who pay union dues as a necessary business expense can deduct them on Schedule C of their federal tax return. The TCJA and OBBBA restrictions apply only to W-2 employees claiming miscellaneous itemized deductions. Which states still allow union dues deductions? New York, California, Pennsylvania, and Minnesota generally allow union dues deductions on state income tax returns. Rules and eligibility vary by state. Workers should check their state tax authority's guidance or consult a tax professional for specifics. Are union dues withheld pre-tax or after-tax in construction payroll? Union dues are withheld after-tax. Federal income tax, state taxes, and FICA are calculated on gross wages first, then union dues are subtracted. Payroll teams should verify that deduction codes are set up as after-tax to avoid understating taxable wages. Can construction contractors deduct union-related costs as business expenses? Yes. Employer contributions to union trust funds (health, pension, training), workers' compensation premiums, and employer payroll taxes on union workers' wages are all deductible as ordinary business expenses. The restriction on deductibility applies to worker-side union membership dues, not employer-side labor costs. References Internal Revenue Service. "General Instructions for Forms W-2 and W-3 (2026)." ​ irs.gov Internal Revenue Service. "Instructions for Schedule C (Form 1040)." ​ irs.gov Internal Revenue Service. "Can I Claim My Expenses as Miscellaneous Itemized Deductions on Schedule A?" ​ irs.gov One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21), Section 70110. July 2025.

title: Small Business Spotlight: Silk City Coffee
summary: Learn how Silk City Coffee, a Webster Bank Small Business Week award winner, is expanding its community-focused cafés while supporting local nonprofits and economic growth.
body_text: Small Business Spotlight: Silk City Coffee Published on July 23, 2026 | 4 min read | Webster Bank Silk City Coffee , a decade-old coffee retailer with locations in Manchester, Conn., and Willimantic, Conn., is one of two second-place prize winners in Webster Bank’s first national Small Business Week contest that attracted participants from New York, Connecticut, Massachusetts, and Rhode Island. The contest winners were unveiled in the first week of May as part of a celebration of Small Business Week. The Silk City Coffee brand was founded in Manchester in 2016 by Tammy Gerhard and Sarah May with their husbands and business partners, Glenn Gerhard and Rob May. After nearly a decade of successful operation, they expanded with a second location in Willimantic, Conn. Today, both retail locations are dedicated to roasting specialty coffee and providing thoughtful service in their communities. We spoke with Tammy and Sarah to learn more about their plans to expand the reach of their business and how the Webster Bank grant funds they won will help their business plans. “With the right support, we can expand our capacity, increase revenue and more fully serve both the local community and the broader downtown ecosystem.” – Sarah May, Co-Owner, Silk City Coffee Q. What are the main challenges to your business? A: As a newer, independently operated business with two locations, we are building revenue and infrastructure. Soon after opening in the center of a vibrant main street in Willimantic, we realized our limited indoor space significantly impacts our ability to fully serve our growing customer base. While our momentum and foot traffic are increasing, particularly with expanded menu offerings, our physical limitations have restricted capacity and sales and held us back. Q. How will you use this money to help grow your business? A: This funding will help us expand our outdoor space in Willimantic. While this location operates under its own budget, it is built on the same community-centered approach established at our original Silk City Coffee shop in Manchester. We want to be a vital and accessible spot in our community for a greater number of people. This grant will help us transform our large back patio, which the town leased to us for $1 per year, and create a welcoming and thoughtfully designed extension of our café. This outdoor space will double the size of our shop, enhancing the overall customer experience. New seating, lighting, and landscaping will allow us to welcome and serve more customers to create a warm, inviting environment for gatherings. Q. How does your business create economic vitality in your community? A: Silk City Coffee is much more than two coffee shop locations. We serve as a gathering place that fosters connections and drives consistent foot traffic. By utilizing both our indoor space and outdoor areas in the Willimantic café, as well as participating in town-wide events, we will help bring more people into the shopping district. This increased activity also supports neighboring businesses and contributes to a more vibrant downtown economy. Every month, at both locations, we partner with local nonprofits through regular “giveback” programs. These programs offer organizations opportunities to raise funds and awareness. We show our support through our Give Back Cookie ($1 from each cookie donated) and we spread the word on our social channels and post a direct donation link on our website. These partnerships keep dollars circulating locally and help by amplifying the impact of organizations already doing important work. Q. In what ways does Silk City Coffee give back to the community? A: Silk City Coffee’s main mission is to create a welcoming and inclusive space where people feel connected and supported. Tammy is an alumna of Eastern Connecticut State University, making the opportunity to open a location just off campus especially meaningful to her. “We are committed to serving students, faculty, and residents by providing not only quality products, but also a space where people feel seen, valued, and connected.” – Tammy Gerhard, Co-Owner, Silk City Coffee Beyond the cafés, Silk City Coffee actively supports local nonprofit organizations by contributing goods and services to further their initiatives. This includes donating merchandise, providing gift cards for fundraisers, and supplying food and coffee for community events. We provide a formal process through which nonprofits can request support, allowing us to consistently and thoughtfully give back to those doing important work. Through these efforts, Silk City Coffee helps raise awareness and strengthen the impact of organizations within the community. Webster Bank is proud to support Silk City Coffee, a specialty coffee business with two locations, as it expands its reach and deepens its commitment to the community.
